title: Provision Docker capability for evidence ladder V2+ (sandbox has no docker)
description: V0 pre-flight discovered the Modal VM sandbox has no docker CLI, daemon, socket, podman, or nerdctl, and no DOCKER_HOST. Ladder steps V2 (live integration), V3 (qualification), V5 (upgrade lane), V6 (TLS lane), V7 (surrealkv lane) all require a Docker server for compose lanes. Options: sandbox image with docker, remote DOCKER_HOST to a docker-capable machine, or run V2+ from another environment against this branch.
notes: In-container docker is a proven dead end in this sandbox (2026-10-13): (1) Rootless dockerd via rootlesskit works — fake getsubids + newuidmap/newgidmap shims in /work/.mercor-home/.dockerdeps/shim, single-uid map, --subid-source=dynamic, mirror.gcr.io registry mirror for the egress-allowlisted sandbox. (2) runc then skips cgroups (Cgroup Driver: none), but container start dies at devpts: 'error mounting devpts ... gid=5: invalid argument' — the kernel requires gid 5 mapped in the userns, and without setuid newuidmap an unprivileged writer can only map its own egid, so gid 5 can never be mapped. No docker-level workaround. (3) Unprivileged bind mounts are blocked (AppArmor), so /etc/subuid cannot be hidden via a mount ns. Conclusion: containers cannot start in this container-runtime sandbox; egress proxy also blocks api.modal.com (curl 000), so a VM-runtime sandbox with dockerd as entrypoint (create-docker-sandbox.py in the same dir) must be created from outside, or SurrealDB must run natively for the env-driven lanes (ACTIVEGRAPH_SURREALDB_TEST_URL).
close_reason: Docker provisioned in both Modal VM sandboxes using clean image im-01M4SM7KEZNBR03W4EYPTHN1H7. Verified Engine 29.9.0, overlay2, Compose 5.6.0, mercor UNIX socket access, BusyBox execution in both VMs, and SurrealDB v3.3.0 execution in isolated validation VM. Persistent worktrees and OpenCode history retained. V3 qualification remains a separate task.

title: Resolve orca-opencode2-status plugin load failure (err_97f42f88) and codify the OpenCode 2 directory-package layout
description: Server log ref err_97f42f88 surfaced an ENOENT against /home/mercor/.config/opencode/plugins/orca-opencode2-status on every fresh reconciliation cycle. Root cause is OpenCode 2.0.27 rejecting single-file plugin paths: the loader does a directory-package probe via stat('<name>') (no extension) and the file-only install of orca-opencode2-status.js had no companion directory. Resolved by packing it as plugins/orca-opencode2-status/index.js with the relative URL on line 1125 corrected from ./orca-opencode2-status-tui/tui.js to ../orca-opencode2-status-tui/tui.js (md5 of resolved target verified identical to source). To make this fix reproducible from the repo this issue also codifies the layout in docs/adr/0004-opencode-plugin-v2-directory-layout.md and a portable installer in scripts/install-opencode-plugins.sh that handles the legacy single-file removal, the directory package placement, and a post-install verification probe.
acceptance_criteria: Plugin loads cleanly as a directory package: server log shows id='/.../orca-opencode2-status' entrypoint='/.../orca-opencode2-status/index.js' with no 'failed to load plugin' WARN line. Future plugin installations routed through scripts/install-opencode-plugins.sh produce the same layout. The internal ORCA_TUI_PLUGIN_ENTRY URL inside the plugin resolves to the existing orca-opencode2-status-tui/tui.js sibling (md5 unchanged).
notes: Three other workspaces (run ids 4da1bb06, 502e2132, 797c5df9, ecfb849d) reported the same root cause; the global fix at ~/.config/opencode/plugins outlives any single workspace. The codification in this repo (ADR + script) is the durable artifact for future plugin authors.

title: TLS lane: transient websocket handshake timeouts under CPU contention
description: Running the live integration suite over wss://127.0.0.1:8011 (pinned 3.3.0, local CA) intermittently fails with client-side 'TimeoutError: timed out while waiting for handshake response'; failing tests vary run to run (0-4 failures) and are clean on repeat and when fewer containers run. Plain ws lane is stable under identical conditions. Likely load/contention-sensitive and possibly related to surrealdb 2.0.0 blocking_ws using connect() without a context manager (DeprecationWarning). Not a deterministic contract failure; record as a known-issue candidate for the TLS exploration lane (V6).
